thread:
maya: Ran the canary batch for raven-lite-int4 + soft-rescue yesterday. Overall throughput looks fine but parse success dropped from 99.6% -> 94.1 for funcall responses. Filing quick notes.

giorgio: ugh. any common pattern in the failures? truncated json or extra text?

maya: mostly truncated JSON arrays and occasional stray `\n` before the object start. Also a cluster where the model returned a top-level string: `\"CALL:open_url\\nhttps://...\"` instead of a json object.

lee: can you paste a minimal failing example (raw model output)?

maya: sure, sample from the canary run (unedited):

```
"Here's the info:\n[\n{\n  \"tool\": \"open_url\",\n  \"args\": {\n    \"url\": \"https://example.com/resource\"\n  }\n}\n"
```

maya: so we got an unterminated array and the whole payload was wrapped in a top-level string token.

sam: that looks like tokenizer/quasi-escape issue after quantization. Maybe the int4 model is producing extra quote tokens at sequence boundaries.

ops-bot: Canary summary uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/canaries/3951234567. parse_success:94.1%, schema_compliance:92.8%, avg_lat_ms: 132

giorgio: interesting that schema_compliance != parse_success — indicates our post-parse schema checks find additional failures even when JSON parsed ok.

lee: repro steps? which prompt template & max_tokens?

maya: prompt: `INVOKE_TOOL:\n{tool_contract}\nUSER_PROMPT:\n...` max_tokens 512, temperature 0.0, kv-cache enabled, batch_size 8

sam: were we using prefix caching? previous builds had a kvprefix optimization for int8 -> int4 onboarding.

maya: yes, kvprefix enabled. I ran a follow-up with kvprefix disabled and parse_success jumped to 98.9% for the same model build.

giorgio: that points to a batching/kvcache boundary tokenization artefact. We should isolate whether it's during decoding or a stray post-processing step.

lee: short mitigation: add a cheap sanitizer that strips wrapping quotes and attempts ndjson repair before handing to schema validator. We already have schema_rescue pipeline but it's behind a flag.

sam: what's the cost impact? if sanitizer adds 1.2ms on average maybe acceptable for Hosted, but Dedicated needs SLO calc.

maya: measured sanitizer cost ~0.9ms on NodeJS worker for these payloads. Could toggle per-customer.

giorgio: longer term we should add a canary variant that toggles kvprefix/batch split to search for token-boundary flips. Also try fixed_seed deterministic sampling to check randomness.

lee: quick experiment: run 1000 samples with kvprefix on vs off, and also with a micro-batch split (batch_size 1 vs 8). I'll schedule a job.

ops-bot: New job created: job/3951234601 - kvprefix-on-vs-off-sweep (1000 samples each). ETA 2h.

sam: also check whether post-quant kernel selection changed the BOS/EOS token handling. We've seen some kernels omit sentinel on last micro-batch.

maya: note: the failures correlate with sequences ending near our 512 cutoff. We should also try increasing soft_max_tokens to 544 to see if fewer truncations.

giorgio: assignables: lee to run sweep and upload raw outputs, maya to push sanitizer behind canary flag and run a short verification, sam to inspect kernel changes between build a37 -> a39.

lee: will do. If sweep shows >1% delta we escalate to runtime team.

maya: pushed sanitizer flag to canary and re-ran 200 samples: parse_success now 97.6. Still not 99.6 but improved.

sam: can you paste one of the sanitizer transformations? We need a reproducible logic for the parser pre-hook.

maya: sanitizer gist (pseudo):

```
// if payload starts and ends with a quote, unescape then try parse
if (payload[0] === '"' && payload[payload.length-1] === '"') payload = JSON.parse(payload);
// attempt NDJSON repair: wrap stray objects into array if trailing commas, add closing bracket if missing
payload = ndjson_repair(payload);
```

sam: ok. That helps but it's heuristic. We should ensure we log every repaired case to evaluate false-positive rescues.

ops-bot: Logged 46 rescue events in last 200 samples. https://ci.internal/redwood/canaries/3951234567/rescue-log

giorgio: final thought: add a contract test harness that runs model variants through a fixed set of edge-case prompts (quotes at boundaries, nested arrays, code fences). Record parse and semantic correctness.

lee: already on it — prototype harness exists in `eng-ml/qa/contract_harness`. I'll wire it to canary pipeline.

maya: ok. short-term plan: keep kvprefix off for this canary until kernel patch; enable sanitizer with verbose logging; run full sweep results from lee.

sam: and file a runtime bug for kernel token boundary handling (link to build diff). I'll draft.

maya: thanks all. will post a follow-up once sweep finishes.

lee: update: sweep job finished, uploaded to the canary link. kvprefix on had 93.8% parse_success, off had 99.0%. attaching heatmap in the job.

giorgio: that's a pretty clear signal. let's roll kvprefix off for int4 onboard until kernel fix. Good catch.

maya: moving the canary to state: mitigated.
